bugs.creator: jaganmn2
bugs.summary: unclear status of group generic function 'matrixOps'

comments.text:
`help("crossprod")` says:

> These are generic functions since R 4.4.0: methods can be written individually or via the `matOps` group generic function; it dispatches to S3 and S4 methods.

Ignoring the typo `s/matOps/matrixOps/`, the sentence seems to claim that `crossprod` and `tcrossprod` dispatch both S3 methods and S4 methods for `matrixOps`.  That's currently not true.

```
> .S3method("matrixOps", "zzz3", function (x, y) "ok")
> setClass("zzz4", contains = "numeric")
> setMethod("matrixOps", c(x = "zzz4", y = "missing"), function (x, y) "ok")
> x3 <- `class<-`(0, "zzz3")
> x4 <- new("zzz4")
> crossprod(x3)
[1] "ok"
> crossprod(x4)
     [,1]
[1,]    0
> tcrossprod(x3)
[1] "ok"
> tcrossprod(x4)
<0 x 0 matrix>
```

So `crossprod` and `tcrossprod` dispatch S3 methods for `matrixOps` but not S4 methods for `matrixOps`.  That is consistent with:

```
> getGroupMembers("matrixOps")
[1] "%*%"
```

If it has been intended since R 4.4 that they would dispatch S4 methods for `matrixOps`, too, then maybe such a change should happen for R 4.6 ... ?

One last discrepancy: `help("S3groupGeneric")` says:

> This group currently contains the matrix multiply `%*%` binary operator only, where at least `crossprod()` and `tcrossprod()` are meant to follow.

It seems that `crossprod` and `tcrossprod` have *already* followed, if both dispatch S3 methods for `matrixOps`, hence perhaps this sentence should be amended now.

In contrast, `help("S4groupGeneric")` seems correct for now, but it would have to be amended, too, should `crossprod` and `tcrossprod` start dispatching S4 methods for `matrixOps`.

comments.text:
For the record, I have been arguing that it would be preferable not to have matrix products in a new group, but instead use left to right internal dispatch as we do for rbind and cbind (and maybe provide a general interface for doing this).
Otherwise, if e.g package A provides a sparse matrix class cA and package B provides a sparse matrix class cB it is impossible to conveniently arrange for the appropriate dispatch when doing a matrix product of cA x and cB y.
(If both A and B provide matrixOps methods, neither will be dispatched to.)
I still think this is what we should change to, perhaps with the matrixOps dispatch as fallback.

(In reply to Kurt Hornik from comment #1)
> Otherwise, if e.g package A provides a sparse matrix class cA and package B
> provides a sparse matrix class cB it is impossible to conveniently arrange
> for the appropriate dispatch when doing a matrix product of cA x and cB y.
> (If both A and B provide matrixOps methods, neither will be dispatched to.)

`%*%`, `crossprod`, and `tcrossprod` all use `chooseOpsMethod` to resolve S3 dispatch ambiguities.  And that is documented behaviour insofar as `help("S3groupGenerics")` says:

> Members of the \[`matrixOps`\] group have the same dispatch semantics (using _both_ arguments) as the `Ops` group.

S4 dispatch ambiguities (if S4 dispatch worked) would be resolved by additional methods for those signatures.

These existing mechanisms seem convenient enough to me ... ?

comments.text:
I don't see how.

Suppose you have two S3 using packages A and B with sparse matrix
classes cA and cB.  Both want to say: 

  For a matrix product of x and y, if x has my class, then use my method.
  Otherwise, if x is dense and y has my class, then use my method.  

(which is what I think we want)

So we need matrixOps.cA and matrixOps.cB, and this will refuse to
dispatch to anything if one argument has class cA and the other has
class cB.

With left-to-right dispatch we could get what I think we want.

Currently, for the left-to-right S3 dispatch that you propose, one needs two methods for `chooseOpsMethod`:

```
.S3method("matrixOps", "cA", function (x, y) "A")
.S3method("matrixOps", "cB", function (x, y) "B")

.S3method("chooseOpsMethod", "cA",
          function (x, y, mx, my, cl, reverse) TRUE)
.S3method("chooseOpsMethod", "cB",
          function (x, y, mx, my, cl, reverse) TRUE)

F <- function (cx, cy) `class<-`(0, cx) %*% `class<-`(0, cy)
G <- expand.grid(cx = list("cA", "cB", NULL),
                 cy = list("cA", "cB", NULL),
                 stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
G$ans <- .mapply(F, G, NULL)
G
```
```
    cx   cy ans
1   cA   cA   A
2   cB   cA   B
3 NULL   cA   A
4   cA   cB   A
5   cB   cB   B
6 NULL   cB   B
7   cA NULL   A
8   cB NULL   B
9 NULL NULL   0
```

If the group generic function `matrixOps` were eliminated and the internal dispatch mechanism for `%*%`, `crossprod`, and `tcrossprod` changed according to your proposal, then S3 class authors would be saved from writing two methods for `chooseOpsMethod` but newly tasked with writing methods for each of `%*%`, `crossprod`, and `tcrossprod`.

From the point of view of **Matrix** maintenance, where we currently have 70-75 S4 methods for each of `%*%`, `crossprod`, and `tcrossprod`, my gut feeling is that an S4 group generic `matrixOps` would simplify things quite a bit.  Well, that is S4, not S3.

It's worth pointing out that I accomplish the same left-to-right S3 dispatch by changing the default method for `chooseOpsMethod`, which returns `FALSE`, to one that returns `TRUE`:

```
.S3method("chooseOpsMethod", "default",
          function (x, y, mx, my, cl, reverse) TRUE)
```

Maybe I should have started discussion on the mailing list ...  On the other hand, it *is* a bug that documentation and behaviour do not agree here.
